facts.text: Vermilion's historic downtown hosts the Vermilion History Museum, which once served as a print shop and weekly newspaper from 1905 to 1964.
The town earned the nickname 'Harbor Town 1837' thanks to Friends of Harbor Town, a nonprofit that highlights Vermilion’s maritime roots.
A walking tour in downtown Vermilion lets visitors step back in time through historic photos of landmarks like the Old Bell Tower and German Tabernacle.
The Vermilion Historical Society preserves the town’s fishing heritage, showcasing techniques from early American Indians to modern Great Lakes commercial fishermen.
Linwood Park, a local treasure, offers a nostalgic experience with historic photos of the Old Bell Tower, Bath House, and merry-go-round.
In 1970s, community-wide revitalization efforts began to preserve Vermilion’s historic qualities, encouraging owners to retain architectural character.
